findings.adjudication: Teach bidirectional TGF: macula-densa NaCl increase -> afferent constriction -> single-nephron GFR down with renin suppression; NaCl decrease -> reduced afferent TGF constriction/support of GFR plus renin/RAAS handoff. Keep TGF distinct from glomerulotubular balance.

Keep exam-useful classical size/charge selectivity, but place nephrin on the podocyte slit-diaphragm structural/permselectivity axis rather than teaching nephrin loss itself as loss of a negative-charge barrier.
Stored-RBC hyperkalemia is taught from storage-lesion extracellular K accumulation/K leakage; citrate-to-bicarbonate is a separate alkalosis route. Hemolysis is not the default sole explanation.

Reject a universal K-H four-grid. Teach normal K/H coupling and require context before urine-pH prediction; type-IV RTA may have urine pH below 5.5 despite reduced net acid excretion, and paradoxical aciduria is context-dependent. Full clinical acid-base/RTA discrimination remains B5 territory.
Preserve low-Mg -> reduced ROMK inhibition -> distal renal K wasting as a useful precision mechanism.

First-pass renin Core is perfusion pressure, beta1 sympathetic input and macula-densa NaCl, plus AngII negative feedback. NO and other context-sensitive low-frequency regulator lists are Source-specific Precision rather than unconditional causal arrows.
